cards.title: PixartualAI vs Framer
cards.desc: A design-first canvas against a prompt-first platform. Where it lands: motion and canvas control versus speed, real data, and apps.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Webflow
cards.desc: Deep control for a specialist against changes anyone can ship. Includes how to move an existing Webflow site over 1:1.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Wix
cards.desc: A drag-and-drop editor with a huge app market against a prompt-first platform. Where it lands: breadth of add-ons versus design quality and real data.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Squarespace
cards.desc: Beautiful templates you fit your content into, against a page generated around your content. Plus what happens when you need more than a site.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs WordPress
cards.desc: The most extensible platform on the web, and the maintenance that comes with it, against one place where nothing needs patching.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Lovable
cards.desc: A codebase you own and maintain against a platform your whole team can run. The difference shows up months after launch.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Replit
cards.desc: A full cloud development environment against a website platform. Where it lands: who has to open the editor after launch.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs v0
cards.desc: Generated components you paste into your own codebase, against a complete site that runs on its own.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs ChatGPT
cards.desc: It can write the code and the copy. It cannot host the site, structure the content, or keep it running.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Claude Code
cards.desc: A coding agent that works in your repository, against a platform that runs the site for people who do not have one.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Codex
cards.desc: A software engineering agent for developers, against a platform that ships and hosts the site itself.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Contentful
cards.desc: A content API that assumes you build the front end, against a platform where the site and the content ship together.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Sanity
cards.desc: A developer-first content backend you shape in code, against a site that arrives already built around your content.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Figma
cards.desc: The industry standard for designing a site, against a platform that produces the working one. Most teams need both.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Unbounce
cards.desc: A conversion-focused landing page tool against a platform that also builds the rest of the site. Where it lands: testing depth versus scope.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Readymag
cards.desc: A free-canvas tool for expressive editorial and portfolio work, against a platform for sites that need to keep running.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Ceros
cards.desc: Interactive campaign content designed to be embedded, against a platform that runs the whole site it sits on.

cards.title: PixartualAI vs Adobe Experience Manager
cards.desc: An enterprise digital experience platform against a tool a small team can actually run. Very different budgets and very different jobs.
